papers_read.title_as_printed: Prediction of future dementia among patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) by integrating multimodal clinical data (Cirincione et al., Heliyon 10 (2024) e36728)

Explainable Machine Learning with Pairwise Interactions for Predicting Conversion from Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease Utilizing Multi-Modalities Data (Cai et al., Brain Sci. 2023, 13, 1535)

what_each_reports.P-156: TADPOLE (ADNI 1/2/GO), 841 baseline EMCI/LMCI patients (286-288 progressed to dementia, 553-555 stayed MCI); outcome is the most recent diagnosis at any later time (no fixed horizon). Ensemble Integration over 9 modalities (cognitive tests, MRI volumes and ROI measures, CSF, demographics/APOE4); 80/20 split, 5-fold nested CV on training. Held-out test: EI AUC 0.81, F-measure 0.68; XGBoost AUC 0.68; autoencoder AUC 0.79.
what_each_reports.P-211: ADNI 1/2/3/GO, 1042 amnestic MCI at baseline; horizon-specific outcomes, conversion to AD (NINCDS-ADRDA, other dementias excluded) within 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 years (5-year analysable n=225: 140 MCI, 85 AD). Explainable Boosting Machine on 21 features (cognitive scores, FreeSurfer hippocampus/amygdala/entorhinal/inferior temporal measures, demographics, APOE4); 90/10 split, SMOTE, 5-fold CV. Five-year accuracy 85%, AUC 0.92 (Comb a, read from Figure 2); AUC about 0.9 at 1 year, lowest at 3 years; 3-year test with interactions AUC 0.81.

quantity_a: AUC for MCI-to-dementia (all-cause, per latest recorded diagnosis, variable follow-up) on a held-out 20% test set, multimodal including CSF
quantity_b: AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion within a fixed 5-year window (AD only), cross-validated EBM with SMOTE, cognitive + regional MRI + APOE4
incompatible_if_same: No. P-211's own horizon-specific AUCs range from its 3-year test value of 0.81 up to about 0.92 at 5 years. P-156's 0.81 sits inside that range, and P-156 gives no interval. The models also differ, and neither paper claims an ordering that the other refutes.

gates.task: match in class (MCI-to-dementia/AD prognosis, the registry's T2), but the endpoints differ: all-cause dementia at the latest visit vs AD within exactly 5 years (P-211 also reports 1-4 years)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (P-156 via TADPOLE ADNI 1/2/GO, P-211 ADNI 1/2/3/GO), so the MCI participants overlap heavily
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal only (V2): P-156 single held-out test; P-211 5-fold CV / 10% test
gates.modality_family: match in broad terms: both multimodal clinical plus structural-MRI ROI features (P-156 adds CSF; neither uses PET features after P-156's missingness filter)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both report ROC-AUC, but the endpoint differs (all-cause dementia at an unfixed horizon vs AD within 5 years, other dementias excluded), and so do the validation scheme (held-out test vs CV with SMOTE) and the sample (841 vs 225 at 5 years)
performance_validity: flag does not apply: both AUCs are below 0.97
independence: Not independent in data: both draw on the same ADNI MCI participants (ADNI 1/2/GO overlap); distinct author groups
grounds: P-156 predicts the latest recorded diagnosis of dementia with no fixed horizon, whereas P-211's 0.92 is for AD conversion within five years with other dementias excluded, so the endpoints differ.

P-211 reports that AUC varies with horizon (about 0.9 at 1 year, lowest at 3 years, where the test AUC is 0.81, and about 0.92 at 5 years), which shows that the 0.81 vs 0.92 gap tracks the horizon choice.
The validation designs differ: P-156 uses a single held-out 20% test, while P-211's figure is cross-validated with SMOTE on the 225 patients who have 5-year data.
The two cohorts are drawn from overlapping ADNI MCI participants, so any comparison would also be non-independent.

evidence_quotes.quote: our target prediction problem was to predict which of these MCI patients' diagnosis changed to dementia, and who stayed as MCI, based only on data collected at baseline
The most recent diagnosis given to each patient (Final DX) was the outcome predicted (stable MCI or progressed to dementia).
on a held out test set, the EI-based model performed better (AUC = 0.81, F-measure = 0.68) than the more commonly used XGBoost (AUC = 0.68, F-measure = 0.57)
The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.
The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects)

record_defects: Registry Sample_N_Approx '242804' for P-211 is not a sample size; the paper includes 1042 aMCI patients (225 with 5-year outcome).
Registry Modality 'MRI/PET' for both is inaccurate: neither uses PET features (P-156 excluded PET modalities for missingness; P-211 uses MRI measures with cognitive/demographic data).
task_equal/dataset_equal treated as full matches without noting the different horizons, or that the MCI participants in the two ADNI cohorts overlap.
The resolution_note bridging list names other studies' scores and no condition separating these two; the horizon difference is the explanation, and it is an incommensurability, not bridging evidence.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-156 result at a fixed 5-year AD-only horizon (or a P-211 result on all-cause dementia at the latest visit) with an interval excluding the other's estimate; neither paper reports one.
